source_figures.original_caption: Figure 3. Effect of fine-tuning on rare-regime adaptation and historical-regime retention. (a) RMSE before and after fine-tuning for historical low-change samples and rare high-change samples. (b) Historical-regime degradation plotted against rare-regime RMSE improvement for different update configurations. The dashed horizontal line indicates the 25% allowable degradation threshold. (c) Layer-freezing comparison showing RMSE for the baseline model, decoder-only fine-tuning, and full-network tuning.

source_figures.original_caption: Figure 4. Comparison of continual-learning strategies for rare-regime adaptation and historical-regime retention using fine tuning (FT), fixed replay, and elastic weight consolidation (EWC). (a) Scalar performance metrics for the baseline U-Net, simple fine-tuning, fixed replay, and elastic weight consolidation (EWC). Metrics include historical-regime RMSE, rare-regime RMSE, rare-regime plume-mass error, rare-regime peak-concentration error, historical-regime Mass90 error, and rare-regime Mass90 error. (b) Stability–plasticity tradeoff for the update strategies, where the x-axis shows rare-regime RMSE improvement and the y-axis shows historical-regime degradation relative to the baseline. Points farther to the right indicate greater rare-regime adaptation, whereas lower points indicate better retention of historical-regime performance. (c) Representative rare-regime plume predictions and error maps for the baseline, simple fine-tuning, fixed replay, and EWC models. Error is computed as predicted minus reference concentration.

source_figures.original_caption: Figure 5. Adaptive replay control and acceptance-region analysis. Panel (a) shows the update trajectory, where the replay ratio (rt) increases in response to historical-regime forgetting and reaches the imposed replay-ratio cap. Panel (b) compares final historical-regime degradation and rare-regime improvement across fixed and adaptive replay controllers. Panel (c) shows the acceptance region defined by maximum allowable historical degradation and minimum required rare-regime improvement, points inside the shaded region satisfy both criteria for surrogate redeployment.
